title: Ind-finite finitely presented algebras over a contractible base are w-strictly local
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative w-contractible ring [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. Let $D$ be a nonempty small directed poset and $(B_d)_{d\in D}$ a direct system of commutative $A$-algebras, with unital $A$-algebra transition maps. Assume each $B_d$ is finite as an $A$-module (generated by a finite list) and finitely presented as an $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Put $B=\varinjlim_d B_d$ in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then $B$ is w-strictly local: its closed points form a closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}B$, every point specializes to exactly one closed point, and every localization at a maximal ideal is strictly henselian [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. Every closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ maps to a closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. The canonical maps induce homeomorphisms
$$(\operatorname{Spec}B)^c\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_d(\operatorname{Spec}B_d)^c,\qquad \pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}B)\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_d\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}B_d),$$
where superscript $c$ denotes the closed-point subspace and $\pi_0$ has the quotient topology [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite]. Zero algebras, empty spectra, and noninjective transition maps are allowed. No assertion that $B$ is w-contractible is made.

proof.text: Write $X_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$. By [lem-ce-finite-finitely-presented-wcontractible], applied with $R=A$ and $S=B_i$, each $B_i$ is w-contractible, hence w-strictly local. Its hypotheses are exactly module finiteness and algebra finite presentation from the item. The equivalence of the two w-local conventions is clause 3 of [det-pe-wlocal-components]; consequently [sk-def-pe-wlocal] gives a unique maximal ideal above every prime of $B_i$, a closed subset $X_i^c$, and strictly henselian maximal localizations.

source.place: Tag 0986, lemma-finite-finitely-presented-over-w-contractible; w-local convention compared by Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.1.4 and Remark 2.1.5.

proof.text: For $i\leq j$, a finite list generating $B_j$ over $A$ also generates it over $B_i$: replace each coefficient $a\in A$ in its generating expression by its image in $B_i$. Thus $B_i\to B_j$ is module-finite, and is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. The induced map $X_j\to X_i$ sends closed points to closed points by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal]. The same argument shows that $A\to B_i$ sends closed points of $X_i$ to closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. None of these arguments assumes an injective transition map.

source.place: Tag 00GK, lemma-finite-is-integral; Tag 00OI, lemma-going-up-maximal-on-top, with integral going-up Tag 00GU.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-filtered-spectrum-topological-limit] to the given nonempty small directed system. It identifies $X$ with the compatible prime families $(\mathfrak p_i)_i$, with the topology induced by the coordinate projections $p_i:X\to X_i$. Inclusion of primes corresponds to coordinatewise inclusion: specialization in this initial topology is coordinatewise specialization, and in an affine spectrum specialization is inclusion of prime ideals (the basic opens are $D(b)$). We use this identification also for families constructed in the next two steps.

source.place: Tags 0CUE and 0CUF, affine cases, as stated by the cited spectrum-limit node.

proof.text: Given $\mathfrak p\in X$, let $\mathfrak p_i$ be its coordinates and let $\mathfrak m_i$ be the unique maximal ideal containing $\mathfrak p_i$ (step 1). The contraction of $\mathfrak m_j$ to $B_i$ is maximal by step 2 and contains $\mathfrak p_i$, so it equals $\mathfrak m_i$. Hence $(\mathfrak m_i)_i$ is compatible. Step 3 supplies a prime $\mathfrak m$ of $B$ with these coordinates and $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m$. This prime is maximal: if a prime $\mathfrak q$ contains it then $\mathfrak q_i\supseteq\mathfrak m_i$ forces equality at every coordinate and then $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m$. There is no larger proper ideal, since any such ideal lies in a maximal ideal by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal].

source.place: Lemma 2.1.9, compatible closed specializations; here expanded using the prime-family description. Maximal existence: Algebra Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology (2).

proof.text:
Every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $B$ has maximal coordinates: apply step 4 with $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak n$; maximality forces $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m$. If $\mathfrak n$ contains a given prime $\mathfrak p$, its coordinates are therefore maximal ideals containing $\mathfrak p_i$ and must equal the $\mathfrak m_i$ from step 4. Thus every point of $X$ has exactly one closed specialization. Moreover,
$$X^c=\bigcap_i p_i^{-1}(X_i^c).$$
The right side is closed, since every $X_i^c$ is closed by step 1. This proves that $B$ is w-local [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. Restricting the prime-family homeomorphism of step 3 gives the asserted homeomorphism $X^c\cong\varprojlim_iX_i^c$: on both sides the topology is generated by the restrictions of the same coordinate inverse images of open subsets of $X_i$.

source.place: Lemma 2.1.9, cofiltered-limit argument and identification of the closed-point subspace; explicit prime-family specialization argument.

proof.text:
For $X$ and each $X_i$, clause 2 of [det-pe-wlocal-components] identifies the closed-point subspace homeomorphically with the quotient space of connected components. These homeomorphisms commute with the transition and projection maps: the component of a closed point maps to the component of its image, and those images are closed by steps 2 and 5. Applying these homeomorphisms coordinatewise to the homeomorphism in step 5 proves
$$\pi_0(X)\cong\varprojlim_i\pi_0(X_i).$$
This is the canonical comparison in the statement, not just an abstract homeomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 2.1.4 and Remark 2.1.5 applied to the limit of Lemma 2.1.9.

proof.text:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be any maximal ideal of $B$. By step 5 its contractions $\mathfrak m_i$ are maximal. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-localization-at-prime],
$$B_{\mathfrak m}\cong\varinjlim_i(B_i)_{\mathfrak m_i},$$
with fraction transition maps $b/s\mapsto\varphi_{ij}(b)/\varphi_{ij}(s)$. These maps are local: a fraction lies in the target maximal ideal exactly when its numerator does, and $\varphi_{ij}^{-1}(\mathfrak m_j)=\mathfrak m_i$. Every source localization is strictly henselian by step 1. Therefore [lem-sfb-filtered-colimit-strictly-henselian-local] applies and makes $B_{\mathfrak m}$ strictly henselian. Together with step 5 this is precisely w-strict locality in [sk-def-pe-wlocal].

source.place: Tag 037D, lemma-colimit-normal-ring, localization identity in its proof; Tag 04GI, lemma-colimit-henselian; Bhatt–Scholze Example 2.2.2.

proof.text: Choose $i\in D$, possible because $D$ is nonempty. Any closed point of $X$ maps to a closed point of $X_i$ by step 5, and then to a closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by step 2; this composite is the structural map. If a stage or the colimit is the zero ring, the empty prime-family space in step 3 and all empty closed-point and component spaces are treated by the same argument; maximal-localization assertions are vacuous for an empty spectrum. No step asserts extremal disconnectedness of the inverse limit.

I read all 8 steps and every cited statement. Step 1: lem-ce (Stacks 0986, proetale.tex l.2028) makes each B_i w-contractible. det-pe-wlocal-components clause 3 converts the component convention into unique closed specialization. Step 2: the A-generators also generate B_j over B_i, so B_i→B_j is module-finite, hence integral, hence maximal ideals contract to maximal ideals. No injectivity is needed. Steps 3-5: lem-a1 gives the prime-family homeomorphism, and specialization is coordinatewise inclusion. The compatible maximal family above p is built from uniqueness at each stage plus integral contraction, and maximality follows from coordinatewise equality and injectivity. X^c=∩p_i^{-1}(X_i^c) is closed, and the restriction to lim X_i^c is well defined because closed points map to closed points. Step 6: det clause 2 identifications are natural, so the comparison is the canonical π0 map. Step 7: the localization-colimit node applies to a directed poset. The fraction maps are local (numerator test), so the new 04GI node gives strictly henselian B_m. Step 8: D is nonempty and the structure map factors through a stage. Small cases checked: separably closed field with finite products, nonreduced finite stages, zero stages. New node lem-sfb-filtered-colimit-strictly-henselian-local is exactly Stacks 04GI (algebra.tex l.42926, strict case) and is self-contained. It is not a restated item clause. rg -L over dag/nodes found no duplicate: filtered-colimit-henselian-pair gives only the pair statement, without locality or a separably closed residue field.
